title: staggered provision window and burst concession gate
author: Ravi Kapoor
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleet churn (rapid scale-ups/downs) and transient microbursts have been contributing noticeable tail latency and cost oscillation in customer workloads. This PR introduces a new autoscaler policy (staggered provision window / windowed-pacing) and a complementary runtime "concession gate" that allows short-lived temporary burst capacity on top of reservations while ensuring accountability via a concession ledger and utilization telemetry. Design goals: reduce unnecessary provisioning churn, avoid starvation during short bursts, maintain per-tenant throughput guarantees, and emit clear telemetry so we can evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs. What changed (high level): 1) autoscaler: windowed_pacer.go implements a staggered provision window algorithm that ramps provisioning actions across configurable time slices instead of immediate all-or-nothing commits. The algorithm computes a provision cadence using recent request-rate slopes and a configured safety margin. 2) concession gate: a lightweight runtime guard (concession_ledger.go + concession_gate.go) that allows tenants to temporarily exceed reserved slots for up to a configured budget/timebox. Concessions are tracked per-tenant and capped; they are reconciled against later provisioning decisions to avoid double-allocations. 3) telemetry: new metrics exported (burst_concession_count, burst_concession_seconds, staged_provision_p90, staged_provision_retries) and a small set of labels to correlate concessions with tenant, pool, and autoscaler-decisions. 4) API/config: new flags in Dedicated config: staged_provision_window_seconds, staged_provision_slices, concession_budget_tokens, concession_timebox_seconds, concession_backoff_jitter. 5) tests and docs: unit tests for windowed pacing, integration test simulating microbursts, and a docs page under docs/dedicated/autoscale-windowed-provision.md describing knobs and operational guidance. Backwards compatibility: all flags default to disabled (zero) so clusters will not change behavior unless operators opt in. Migration: enabling staged provision requires restarting autoscaler controllers; concession ledger persists to existing reservation metadata store, and a migration step is provided in the installer notes. Rollout plan: opt-in in staging for 2 weeks with telemetry collection, gradual rollout to low-traffic fleets, and monitoring alerts on staged_provision_retries and unexpected concession drain. The description below includes the commit summary, changed files and a distilled review conversation. The goal of this PR is a conservative, observable mechanism for tempered autoscaling that reduces scale thrash while giving workloads safe burst headroom.

review_comments: Alex Morales: Overall looks good. Two asks before approving: (1) add a telemetry label that ties concession records back to the autoscaler decision id; (2) ensure concession_timer uses monotonic clock (I think time.Since on system time is used in one spot).

Ravi Kapoor (author): Addressed both: added decision_id label on burst_concession_count and switched to time.Now().Sub with clock.Now monotonic wrapper in concession_gate.go. Pushed fix in commit f3a4b11.

Priya Singh: Need stronger bounds on concession_budget_tokens default. Suggested lowering default from 100 to 10 and adding a circuit-breaker that disables concessions for tenants with repeated evictions.
Ravi Kapoor: Changed default to 10, added eviction_count check to concession_gate.go and a unit test that asserts concession deny after 3 evictions.

Nate Kim: CI failed on lint initially, and there was a flake in the integration test where staging provisioning slices were zero. Confirmed fixed by adding a retry harness and tightening the timing windows.
Release manager (internal): Please add a short release note mention and include expected signal names for alerting.

release_notes: Introduce a staged provision window autoscaler (opt-in) plus a concession gate that allows short bursts beyond reservations. New telemetry: burst_concession_count, burst_concession_seconds, staged_provision_p90. Defaults disabled; operators must enable via dedicated config flags. Recommended opt-in in staging and monitor staged_provision_retries and concession drain metrics.
operational_playbook_snippet: If you enable staged provision, monitor 'telemetry.staged_provision_retries' and 'telemetry.burst_concession_seconds'. If retries spike >5% for 15m, disable staged_provision_window_seconds or increase staged_provision_slices. For sustained high concession usage, increase reservation commits or tune concession_budget_tokens and concession_timebox_seconds.
notes_for_sre: SRE: this feature may change provisioning cadence. We recommend enabling on a single low-utilization pool first. The concession ledger is stored with reservation metadata; backups are supported via the existing reservation snapshot job. Expect a small increase in short-lived allocation churn while the algorithm learns rate slopes.
